versions.changelog: Trigger constraints move into the manifest. The claw.json description now says when NOT to reach for this skill - a quick 2D page game, a downloadable Unreal title, store submission or certification, or a shipped game's fight balance - matching the entry document's own scope sections, which answers the SQP-1 finding. This release follows 1.1.3, where the GPU-parking guidance became an operator decision (both scanners asked for exactly that) and the entry doc stopped naming its own filename, clearing the last AE1: clawscan, the AI scanner and static analysis are clean and skillspector sits at LOW/12. Checker 9 of 9.

GPU parking is now the operator's decision, not the agent's - the guidance names the process holding the card and asks, running the park/restore sequence only on their agreement, in the editor page and the traps page alike (both scanners asked for exactly this, and clawscan's guidance is explicit about approval). The entry doc no longer names its own filename, which was the last AE1 literal a scanner cannot resolve. Checker 9 of 9; the remaining finding is the MIT-0 licence text, read as granted agency.

Fixes the causes the 1.1.1 scan exposed rather than its counts. AE1 fired on unresolvable file references - a bare filename and a glob - so every artifact is now named by its shipped path. LP3 wanted permissions declared in the entry doc itself: the frontmatter now carries a permissions block (no network, own-folder read, one append to the art log, no shell, no subprocess, no install, no publish) and an allowed-tools list. A contradiction I introduced in the asset reference is reworded, the Poly Haven API URL literal is gone, and the GPU-parking note is scoped to the editor run. Checker 9 of 9.

Answers the audit's two HIGHs. The self-check is now disclosed in the description and bounded: it audits this package's own text only and never reads the caller's project or repository. New 'Scope, permissions and limits' section states what the package reads, runs and writes, what it never does, and the allowed-tools list a host should grant; the asset reference now says outright that its hosts are for the reader's agent to browse and that no shipped script opens a socket. The entry doc is 14,850 bytes, inside the scanner's inspection window - the former AE1 'SKILL.md (partial)' - with every removed line living in the reference page that already owned it. Checker passes 9 of 9.

Broadened from a Battle TV style guide into an agent's Unity guide: engine install, template projects, the unity CLI/MCP bridge, 2D-vs-3D stage decisions, CC0 asset sourcing with a licence gate, and the WebGL build-serve-verify loop. Adds references/ (getting-started, editor-cli, 2d-and-3d, assets-and-licences, webgl-shipping, traps) and scripts/check_skill.py with 9 named self-check rules. The Battle TV style and its living art log are preserved whole as references/battle-tv-style.md and references/techniques.md.
Remove local drive paths and user folders. Public tutorial only. Home https://chatagent.ca/
Initial public release. Painted Battle TV style. Home https://chatagent.ca/
